name: setlist-drag-reorder
note: Setlist rows are ALWAYS reorderable and removable - there is no edit mode. REWRITTEN 2026-07-26 (SONGS-MERGE phase 1): this scenario asserted the RETIRED edit-mode contract (#setEdit revealing up/dn arrows, a body-tap that must NOT open while arranging). #setEdit has not existed for some time, so the scenario was failing on main and guarding nothing - a dead guard on the setlist, found while merging Library+Setlist. It now asserts today's contract: drag from the grip reorders and persists, and a body tap always opens the song. UPDATED 2026-10-06: S-SETLIST-GESTURES (#342) retired the .li-grip handle - the ROW itself lifts for reorder (press-and-hold on touch, movement-lift on mouse), so the drags start from the row body. setlist-gestures.json proves the gesture mechanics (incl. swipe-delete); THIS scenario keeps the reorder OUTCOME contract it alone carries: the order PERSISTS to storage both directions, the position numbers re-render, and a body tap still opens the song.

steps.label: today's contract (S-SETLIST-GESTURES, #342): no resting grip and no edit-mode toggle - every row is itself the drag surface (swipeable .li-inner)
prep the drag: scroll the set into view, clear any stray text selection
RED GOALPOST: row 1 dragged below row 3 - the setlist PERSISTS as k1,k2,k0 (order is the content here, so it has to survive the write)
the visible position numbers follow the new order (1,2,3 top to bottom, not a stale render)
prep the drag: scroll the set into view, clear any stray text selection
dragging the last row back above the first restores k0,k1,k2
a body tap ALWAYS opens the song now - there is no arrange-only mode in which it must not
